title: Hex.pm package registry breach, Nov 2026

subject.name: Hex.pm
subject.about: Hex is the package manager for languages that run on the BEAM virtual machine, such as Elixir and Erlang: developers use hex.pm to publish and download code packages. It is open source and is run by Six Colors AB, a Swedish company that charges for private packages.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Hex, Six Colors AB, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: Hex is where Elixir and Erlang developers worldwide get their packages; it says it serves millions of packages daily. What is known: commands ran on six servers for about 13 minutes. Whether account data was read is not known, and Hex has given no number of accounts.
who_is_affected: People with a hex.pm account: Hex asks them to change their password, set up 2FA again and update their Hex client when the new release is out. Organisations with private packages will hear from Hex if affected. Developers who only download public packages have nothing to reset.

known.text: Hex says an attacker used a flaw in hex.pm to run commands on six of its web servers on Nov 23, 2026.
Hex cannot rule out that email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes and 2FA secrets were read.
Hex replaced its server credentials and signing keys and signed everyone out.
Hex reported it to the Swedish data protection authority, CISA and ENISA.
